title: New Tax Regime: Key Deductions & Exemptions You Can No Longer Claim
description: The new income tax regime, introduced from FY 2020-21, offers lower tax rates across various income slabs. However, opting for this regime means foregoing ove.

faq.q: Is the new tax regime mandatory for everyone?
faq.a: No, the new tax regime is not mandatory. While it is the default option from FY 2023-24, individual taxpayers can still choose to opt for the old tax regime annually.

faq.q: Can I switch between the old and new tax regimes every year?
faq.a: Yes, salaried individuals can opt for the old or new tax regime each financial year when filing their Income Tax Return. However, individuals with business income have more restrictive rules for switching.

faq.q: What are the main benefits of the new tax regime?
faq.a: The main benefits are lower tax slab rates and a simpler tax structure, as it eliminates the need to track and claim numerous deductions and exemptions. A standard deduction of ₹50,000 is also available for salaried individuals and pensioners.

faq.q: Are there *any* deductions allowed in the new tax regime?
faq.a: Yes, a few deductions are still allowed. These include the standard deduction of ₹50,000 for salaried individuals and pensioners, employer's contribution to NPS (Section 80CCD(2)), and certain deductions related to Agniveer Corpus Fund.

faq.q: Who benefits most from the new tax regime?
faq.a: Individuals with lower incomes, those who don't make many tax-saving investments, or those who don't claim significant deductions like HRA or home loan interest, often find the new regime more beneficial due to its lower tax rates.

faq.q: What happens if I don't choose a regime?
faq.a: If you are a salaried individual and do not explicitly communicate your choice to your employer, the new tax regime will be applied by default for TDS purposes. However, you can still choose your preferred regime when filing your Income Tax Return.
